risks.description: Exclusion of vulnerable groups (such as women, illiterate citizens, persons with disabilities, and isolated rural populations) from registering in the NPR and SR due to inadequate outreach or complex processes.
risks.mitigation: Mobilize Citizen Service Centers (CSCs), deploy mobile units with satellite connectivity in isolated areas, and implement an inclusive Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP) paired with a dedicated Grievance Mechanism.
risks.evidence: Section IV.D, paragraph 85: Potential negative social impacts from project activities are mainly related to the exclusion of some vulnerable groups due to inefficient or inadequate public communication.

risks.description: Unintended disclosure or breach of sensitive biographic and biometric data collected within the National Population Registry and Social Registry.
risks.mitigation: Enforce strict compliance with national data privacy laws (Law 09-08), integrate privacy-by-design architecture, perform system enhancements, and train operational staff handling personal data.
risks.evidence: Section IV.D, paragraph 85: Potential negative social impacts from project activities are mainly related to... data protection issues.

risks.description: Improper disposal and environmental contamination from electronic waste generated by deployed mobile units and IT devices.
risks.mitigation: Apply sustainable public procurement principles and adhere strictly to established e-waste management procedures within Ministry of Interior asset management frameworks.
risks.evidence: Section IV.D, paragraph 85: Risks associated with the use of electronic devices (such as mobile units) include the potential generation of e-waste and its improper disposal.

risks.description: Reluctance among informal sector workers to register in the social registries due to fears that personal data will be used for tax enforcement.
risks.mitigation: Execute tailored communication and public outreach campaigns explaining the sole social protection purpose of registration and building public trust in the system.
risks.evidence: Section II.G, paragraph 53: some strata of the population, such as workers in the informal sector, are wary of providing their information to the government due to perceived risks.

risks.description: Seasonal and annual income instability among agricultural and non-salaried workers leading to contribution defaults under mandatory social insurance programs.
risks.mitigation: Establish dynamic welfare scoring and dynamic SR updating mechanisms to quickly identify vulnerable workers experiencing shocks and provide targeted social contribution support.
risks.evidence: Section I.B, paragraph 13: Several categories of non-salaried workers, in particular farmers... suffer from two patterns of irregularities in the flow of income... affecting ability to pay.

risks.description: Institutional delays and capacity constraints in fully operationalizing the National Registry Agency (NRA) while simultaneously expanding the NPR and SR.
risks.mitigation: Provide technical assistance under Sub-component 1.3 and utilize Performance-Based Conditions (PBC 4) to ensure key NRA leadership recruitment, approval of operational manuals, and smooth transfer of management responsibilities.
risks.evidence: Section II.G, paragraph 52: This rapid expansion has strained the government’s and the MoI’s capacity to take steps in operationalizing the NRA.

risks.description: Delays and quality errors in Financial Management reporting caused by manual spreadsheet processing and data extraction from national budget software.
risks.mitigation: Develop, install, and operationalize automated financial management software to generate accurate Interim Financial Reports and annual project financial statements.
risks.evidence: Section IV.B, paragraph 69: the use of a spreadsheet 'Excel'... may lead to some challenges in terms of quality and timeliness in the preparation of IFRs.

risks.description: Risk of double-counting or duplicating expenditure justifications under the same budget line ('AMO-TADAMON') across overlapping World Bank operations.
risks.mitigation: Create distinct budget codes within the Ministry of Interior budget dedicated specifically to tracking and reporting project-related Eligible Expenditures Programs.
risks.evidence: Section IV.B, paragraph 69: risk of duplication or overlap due to the use of the same budget line 'AMO-TADAMON' to justify expenditure.

risks.description: Severe recurrent climatic events, such as droughts, threatening rural livelihoods and increasing economic vulnerability across target populations.
risks.mitigation: Utilize geographical location data in the NPR and welfare data in the SR to enable rapid, adaptive social protection responses to climate-impacted households.
risks.evidence: Section I.A, paragraph 3: climate-related shocks, primarily droughts, represent significant risks to the Moroccan economy.

risks.description: Data inaccuracies, fraud, or corrupt practices in social registration data undermining social assistance eligibility assessments.
risks.mitigation: Develop and deploy an end-to-end Error, Fraud, and Corruption (EFC) monitoring system and mitigation strategy combined with cross-agency administrative data verification.
risks.evidence: Section II.B, paragraph 30: design and develop an end-to-end Error, Fraud, and Corruption (EFC) monitoring system and EFC mitigation strategy to reduce its rate.

risks.description: Incomplete or delayed capture of deceased registrants in the National Population Registry, leading to ghost beneficiaries and database corruption.
risks.mitigation: Build an automated data exchange system between civil registration offices and the NPR to instantly sync death records and deactivate deceased profiles.
risks.evidence: Section II.B, paragraph 33: removal of deceased registrants is equally important to ensure sustained efficiency.

risks.description: Targeting errors (inclusion and exclusion) resulting from an outdated or inaccurate proxy-means test scoring formula.
risks.mitigation: Conduct process evaluations and empirical studies using household survey data to update and re-calibrate the SR intake questionnaire and welfare scoring formula.
risks.evidence: Section II.B, paragraph 43: develop a strategy to reduce potential exclusion and inclusion errors.

risks.description: Suboptimal working conditions or lack of grievance channels for contracted non-civil-servant project workers.
risks.mitigation: Apply ESS2 labor management standards across all procurement, incorporate worker codes of conduct, and provide dedicated worker grievance redress mechanisms.
risks.evidence: Section IV.D, paragraph 88: Gap-filling measures... have been included in the ESCP to ensure appropriate labor and working conditions in the event that contracted workers are hired.

risks.description: Severe basic infrastructure deficits in remote civil registry offices obstructing the automated issuance of Digital Civil and Social Identifiers (DCSIDs) for newborns.
risks.mitigation: Invest in foundational IT infrastructure, hardware, and digital network upgrades across all 2,200 local Civil Registry Offices nationwide.
risks.evidence: Section II.B, paragraph 32: Civil Registry Offices... in very isolated areas... require substantial investments in overall infrastructure, beyond the needs of new hardware and software.

risks.description: Inter-ministerial misalignment or slow multi-agency coordination delaying system interoperability and strategic decision-making.
risks.mitigation: Maintain active governance under the high-level Inter-ministerial Steering Committee (IMSC) chaired by the MoI Wali Secretary General to oversee policy alignment and enforce cross-agency agreements.
risks.evidence: Section III.A, paragraph 57: The IMSC was maintained... to ensure coordination between the different stakeholders and approval of strategic decisions.
